title: reaper tenant manifest, schema version 1
description: The entire integration surface between a project and reaper. See docs/tenants.md. Two schemas live in this file: the root schema validates the document as written, and $defs/resolvedGuest validates each guest after top-level defaults have been merged with that guest's overrides. The second pass is where execution-mode coherence is enforced, because inheritance is not something JSON Schema can compute.

project.description: Names the working directory under tank/work and the session. Not an identifier the framework attaches any meaning to.

guests.description: Which registered guests this project runs on. Names are resolved against the sysadmin's registry; the framework attaches no meaning to them and deliberately does not validate against a list of known operating systems.

profiles.description: Named variations on a session. A profile changes how a session is run, never what is run.

name.description: Lowercase, starts alphanumeric. Deliberately narrow: these names end up in paths, dataset names and session identifiers.

imageRef.description: A fully-qualified, digest-pinned image reference. Tags are rejected: a run that cannot say which bytes it ran is a run whose result stops meaning anything tomorrow. The first component must actually be a registry host -- dotted, or localhost, with an optional port -- because `library/rust` passing as a host is exactly the ambiguity this field exists to remove. Path components are lowercase because every real registry refuses anything else, and a reference that validates here and fails at pull time helps nobody.

execMode.description: container: commands run in a digest-pinned toolchain image, and the guest template stays generic. host: commands run directly in the guest, with the toolchain supplied by the template. See docs/tenants.md for the tradeoff.

env.description: Environment passed through to the command. Values are strings; the framework does not interpolate, expand or interpret them.

buildPartial.description: Build configuration. Partial: any key may be omitted here and supplied by a per-guest override, or the other way round. Completeness is enforced on the resolved form, not on this one.

cache.description: Names of cache directories under tank/cache, preserved between runs. Free-form: these are the tenant's own labels and the framework attaches no meaning to them.

exec.description: Overrides the guest's execution mode for this verb alone. A project may perfectly reasonably need a pinned toolchain to build and the guest's own container engine to run -- a toolchain image has no engine client inside it.

runPartial.description: Run configuration. Partial, for the same reason as buildPartial.

cmd.description: Opaque. The framework hands this to a shell and does not know what a stage, a journey or a seed is.

images.description: Images pre-pulled into tank/images before the run. Optional and may be empty -- a project that runs no containers declares none.

exec.description: Overrides the guest's execution mode for this verb alone. A project may perfectly reasonably need a pinned toolchain to build and the guest's own container engine to run -- a toolchain image has no engine client inside it.

image.description: The image `run.cmd` executes in. Under container execution this defaults to build.image, so a project whose build and run share one toolchain declares the digest once.

items.description: Only `state` is a rollback target. work, cache and images are refused here rather than left for the runner to notice: work carries results outward, and rolling back cache or images would silently destroy the thing that makes the next iteration fast.

disk_gb.description: Size of the session's storage pool, in gibibytes. Optional; the site's default applies when absent. This is the pool the build caches and the tenant's state live on, so a project with a large cache wants more than the default.

ttl.description: How long a session lives without a heartbeat. Measured from readiness, not from the create request.

warm_cache.description: false runs without tank/cache mounted: determinism mode, for when a warm cache is the suspect.

guestEntry.description: Either a bare registered guest name, or an object overriding the top-level defaults for that guest.

resolvedGuest.description: One guest after top-level defaults have been merged with its own overrides, and after each verb's execution mode and image have been resolved. This is the form the runner actually acts on, and the only form in which execution-mode coherence can be checked -- a manifest may perfectly reasonably declare `exec` at the top level and `build.image` per guest, so neither key alone tells you whether the pair is coherent.

exec.description: This verb's execution mode, resolved: its own if it declared one, otherwise the guest's.

allOf.description: Container execution needs a toolchain image, and it must be declared rather than assumed.
Host execution has no image to run in. An image alongside host execution means one of the two is a mistake, and failing here is far kinder than failing deep inside a guest.

exec.description: This verb's execution mode, resolved: its own if it declared one, otherwise the guest's.

allOf.description: Container execution needs a toolchain image, and it must be declared rather than assumed. Resolution has already copied build.image across where run inherits it, so an absent image here means none was declared anywhere.
Host execution has no image to run in. An image alongside host execution means one of the two is a mistake, and failing here is far kinder than failing deep inside a guest.

sync.description: How the working tree is copied into a session. Optional; without it the whole tree goes.

exclude.description: rsync patterns kept out of the forward sync. `out/` at the top of the tree is always excluded whatever is written here: it is the channel results come back on, and mirroring deletions into it would destroy them. A leading slash anchors a pattern at the top of the tree.
